title: GSA CALC+ Labor Ceiling Rates (Quick Rate API)
agency: U.S. General Services Administration, Federal Acquisition Service
questions: what do GSA schedule contractors charge per hour for a data scientist
ceiling rates for a labor category by education and experience
median hourly rate for software engineers on GSA MAS contracts
all labor rates on one GSA contract
rates of small versus other-than-small businesses

manual.how: Open each link in manual_download/INSTRUCTIONS.md in a browser: each downloads a CSV export (ceilingrates_results.csv) of every matching rate; rename it to the name shown and upload. Without the links: search at https://buy.gsa.gov/pricing/ (CALC+ Labor Ceiling Rates), set the filters, use Export to CSV, and upload the file.

cache.why: The index is rebuilt every night (the _timestamp column), so data/ is reused only within a run.

redistribution.why: CALC+ ceiling rates are published by GSA, a U.S. government agency; federal government works are in the public domain (17 U.S.C. 105) and GSA's website policies place its content in the public domain unless noted.

citation: U.S. General Services Administration, CALC+ Labor Ceiling Rates ({dataset}), api.gsa.gov/acquisition/calc/v3, retrieved {retrieved_long}.

audit_hooks.why: CALC+ rates are awarded ceiling (maximum) prices on schedule contracts, not prices actually paid or wages; a report must say so.

clarify: Which labor categories, exactly? Titles are free text set by each vendor ('Data Scientist III', 'Sr. Data Scientist'): use a keyword search and say how titles were grouped.
Which filters change the comparison: education, minimum years of experience, worksite (customer, contractor, virtual), business size? Default: none, and report the mix.
Current-year price or next/second option-year prices? Default: current_price.
